name: Enckboaz Website Audit
author: enckboaz

sections.description:
Enckboaz Website Audit is visual feedback and task collection on top of any page of your WordPress site. Stop chasing vague emails and blurry screenshots: your clients and teammates click directly on the element that’s wrong, write what they need, and it becomes a trackable task — complete with an automatic screenshot and full technical context.

Built for web agencies and freelancers who collect revisions from clients.

How it works

  1. Open any page of your site while logged in (as a user with review permission).
  2. Click the “Avvia revisione” button in the bottom-right corner.
  3. Click the element you want to report.
  4. Write a title, description and priority.
  5. Done — Enckboaz Website Audit automatically captures the screenshot, the exact CSS element, the URL, browser, OS, device type and viewport size, and files it as an assignable task.

Key features

  • Element picker — highlight and click any text, image, button or section on the live site.
  • Automatic screenshot of the viewport with the reported element highlighted (no browser extension, runs client-side).
  • Automatic context capture — URL, CSS selector, browser + version, OS, device type, viewport, timestamp.
  • Task dashboard — open / in progress / in review / done, with filters and search.
  • Projects — organise tasks per site or per client.
  • Assignments, comments (incl. internal notes), attachments and activity history.
  • Email notifications for new, assigned and completed tasks.
  • Privacy by design — the overlay and admin area load only for authorised reviewers. Normal visitors never load a single byte.

Free and open source — unlimited projects and tasks, with every feature included.

Source code and build process

This plugin ships both the compiled assets in build/ and the unminified
sources they are generated from, so everything can be reviewed and rebuilt.

  • Sources: resources/ (TypeScript and React)
  • Build configuration: vite.config.ts, tsconfig.json, package.json
  • Output: build/

To rebuild the assets from source you need Node.js 18 or later:

npm install
npm run build

npm run build type-checks with `tsc --noEmit` and then bundles with Vite,

writing the result to build/. npm run dev rebuilds on change.

Third-party libraries

The bundles in build/ include the following GPL-compatible libraries, all
installed from npm and listed in package.json:

  • html2canvas 1.4.1 (MIT) — https://github.com/niklasvh/html2canvas
  • React and React DOM 18.3.1 (MIT) — https://github.com/facebook/react
  • React Router 6 (MIT) — https://github.com/remix-run/react-router
  • Radix UI primitives (MIT) — https://github.com/radix-ui/primitives
  • lucide-react (ISC) — https://github.com/lucide-icons/lucide
  • clsx, tailwind-merge, class-variance-authority (MIT)
  • Tailwind CSS 4 (MIT) — https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss
sections.installation:
1. Upload the enckboaz-website-audit folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the ZIP via Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress.
  3. Open Enckboaz Website Audit in the admin menu.
  4. Click the info (ℹ) button in the sidebar for the in-app quick guide.
sections.faq:
Who can create and see tasks?

Only logged-in users with the review capability (administrators and editors by default). Regular site visitors don’t see or load the overlay.

Does it send my data to an external service?

No. Screenshots are generated in the browser and stored in your own WordPress media library. No third-party service is required.

Where are tasks stored?

In dedicated tables in your WordPress database. Uninstalling the plugin removes them.

Does the screenshot need a browser extension?

No. Capture runs fully client-side.
